title: C1625 — Camshaft Position Bank 2 Sensor 2 (CMP22)
introduction:
I use this reference to connect the camshaft sensor’s identity, its cavity drawing and its circuit descriptions. Start with the identification table, find a cavity label in the drawing, then read across the matching Cavity row. Think of the drawing as a seating plan: position finds the seat; the row tells you who belongs there.

This guide supports reference reading. Access, probing, wire selection and replacement require their own procedures. The physical viewing side, test conditions, gauge convention and meanings of Size and Used are unspecified here.

edits.why: I use the vertically stacked cavity labels and the rectangular feature on the drawing’s right as landmarks on the page. The table beneath associates that drawing with its Fpn and harness entry. Together with the identification table above, these details establish which connector record you are reading.

edits.text: Read the cavity and circuit assignments
edits.why: Follow each drawn cavity label to its matching Cavity row, then read horizontally through Circuit Number, Color, Gauge and Function. The function descriptions distinguish the camshaft sensor connection from the variable-reluctance sensor return associated with the powertrain controller. Circuit Number identifies the electrical path; Terminal Part Number identifies the contact part. Keeping those roles separate makes the table useful when reading a circuit reference.

I connect Kit List in the identification table to Number in the pigtail table. Within that row, Service Part is the service reference, Image names the associated illustration file, and Engineering Shell links back to Hard Shell and Fpn. Gauge, Material and Cavities describe the listed pigtail. This keeps the pigtail assembly, connector shell and individual terminal references from becoming a jumble of look-alike part numbers.
